Tecpetrol SA Launches New Oil Recovery Technology in Argentina

BUENOS AIRES, June 14—Argentine oil and gas producer Tecpetrol SA unveiled a new oil recovery technology on Friday, aiming to boost production efficiency at its Neuquén Basin operations.

The company introduced its proprietary Enhanced Oil Recovery (EOR) system at a launch event in Buenos Aires attended by industry executives and government officials. Tecpetrol SA said the technology, which uses polymer flooding methods to extract more crude from mature reservoirs, represents a significant advance for the country’s energy sector. The company plans to deploy the system across several of its fields in the Vaca Muerta region this year.

“We are very proud to present this innovation, developed by our team of Argentine engineers and geologists,” said Tecpetrol SA CEO María López. “This technology will help us make better use of existing resources, lower operational costs, and support Argentina’s goal of increasing energy self-sufficiency.”

According to company figures, pilot tests at the El Tordillo site increased recovery rates by approximately 18 percent compared to traditional water flooding methods. Tecpetrol SA expects the new system will add up to 7,000 barrels per day of incremental production at full rollout.

Energy analysts said the technology could help bolster Argentina’s position as a regional oil producer. “Enhanced recovery is essential as the industry matures,” said Juan Pérez, an analyst at the Buenos Aires-based consultancy Energía Futura. “Tecpetrol’s results are promising and could encourage further investment.”

Government officials welcomed the development, citing its potential to create local jobs and strengthen the domestic supply chain. “Innovations like this are key to the sustainable growth of our oil and gas industry,” said Martín Cardozo, Undersecretary for Hydrocarbons.

The Argentine Oil and Gas Workers Union also expressed support, with Secretary-General Silvia Romero noting, “Our members are committed to working with new technologies that secure long-term employment and responsible resource use.”

Tecpetrol SA said it will continue collaborating with local suppliers and universities to expand the technology’s application in other regions.
